key_insight: High-order discontinuous Galerkin spectral element simulations of a two-dimensional scramjet agree with reference finite-volume solvers for complex hypersonic flow with shock–shock interactions.
engineering_relevance: DGSEM offers an alternative to conventional second-order finite-volume methods for modeling high-enthalpy propulsion flows where numerical dissipation can demand refined meshes.
method: Use high-order DGSEM with element-local polynomial bases.
Compare results against reference finite-volume solvers.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports agreement with reference finite-volume results, supporting implementation verification, but gives no quantitative error or runtime metrics.
watch_item: The reported two-dimensional comparison does not establish computational savings or accuracy for three-dimensional turbulent flows.
paper_title: Efficient high-order Discontinuous Galerkin simulations of multi-species high-enthalpy flows
